hook.text: Engineered bacteria that live in your gut and produce medicine — living therapeutics turn microbes into pharmacies.

buildup.text: Synlogic programs E. coli Nissle to consume phenylalanine — treating phenylketonuria from inside the intestine.

discovery.text: Genetic circuits detect inflammation markers and release anti-inflammatory cytokines locally — precision where pills cannot reach.

twist.text: Biocontainment is essential — kill switches ensure engineered bacteria die if they escape the gut.

climax.text: Phase 2 trials show living therapeutics reducing disease markers — the field moves from proof-of-concept to clinic.

punchline.text: Bacteria as medicine — living therapeutics are programmable drugs.

quiz.question: What is a kill switch in living therapeutics?
options: A mechanism that destroys pathogens in the gut
A genetic circuit that causes engineered bacteria to die if they leave their intended environment
A drug that patients take to stop the therapy

details.summary: Living therapeutics are engineered microorganisms programmed to detect disease signals within the body and respond by producing drugs locally at the site of disease. These smart medicines combine sensing, logic, and therapeutic delivery in a single living system.
details.whyItMatters: Conventional drugs distribute throughout the body, causing side effects. Living therapeutics target disease sites with high precision, produce drugs continuously on demand, and can be programmed to self-destruct when treatment is complete.
takeaways: Engineered bacteria sense disease biomarkers and produce drugs at disease sites
Programmable logic enables conditional drug delivery in response to signals
Clinical trials are testing living therapeutics for cancer and inflammatory disease

faq.question: How do living therapeutics know when and where to deliver drugs?
faq.answer: Genetic circuits include sensor modules that detect disease-specific signals like tumor hypoxia, inflammation markers, or pathogen molecules. When sensors activate, they trigger production and secretion of therapeutic proteins, peptides, or small molecules only at the disease site.

faq.question: What safety mechanisms prevent engineered bacteria from growing uncontrollably?
faq.answer: Kill switches terminate bacteria when they leave the target environment. Auxotrophic strains require nutrients only available in the body or supplied externally. Genetic safeguards ensure population control. Multiple redundant safety layers address regulatory biosafety requirements.
